lessons.title: What is Claude?
lessons.content:
Welcome to Claude for Beginners!

Claude is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. Think of it as a very capable text-based tool you can have a conversation with.

You can ask Claude to:
- Answer questions
- Write and edit text
- Explain complex topics simply
- Help you brainstorm ideas
- Review and improve your writing

Over the next few lessons, you'll learn how to get the most out of Claude — starting with the basics and building up to practical workflows.

Your first challenge: Open Claude (claude.ai) and say hello. Ask it something simple, like 'What's the capital of France?' and see what happens.

lessons.title: Writing Your First Prompt
lessons.content:
A prompt is what you type to Claude. The quality of your prompt directly affects the quality of Claude's response.

Basic prompt structure:
1. Context — tell Claude what the situation is
2. Task — tell Claude what you want it to do
3. Format — tell Claude how you want the answer

Example (weak prompt):
'Write something about dogs.'

Example (strong prompt):
'Write a 3-sentence summary about Labrador Retrievers for a first-time dog owner. Use simple language.'

Key tip: Be specific. The more context you give, the better the result.

Challenge: Ask Claude to explain something you're curious about. Try both a vague version and a specific version. Notice the difference.

lessons.title: Giving Claude a Role
lessons.content:
One of the most powerful techniques is telling Claude who to be.

Instead of: 'Explain machine learning'
Try: 'You are a patient teacher explaining machine learning to a 12-year-old. Use simple words and a real-world analogy.'

Roles you can use:
- 'You are an expert copywriter...'
- 'You are a friendly customer support agent...'
- 'You are a strict code reviewer...'
- 'You are a Socratic tutor who only asks questions...'

Why it works: Claude adjusts its tone, vocabulary, and depth to match the role you assign.

Challenge: Ask Claude the same question twice — once normally, once with a role. Compare the outputs.

lessons.title: Multi-Turn Conversations
lessons.content:
Claude remembers everything said earlier in a conversation. This is called context.

You can:
- Ask follow-up questions: 'Can you expand on point 2?'
- Correct Claude: 'That's not quite right — I meant X, not Y'
- Build on previous answers: 'Now turn that into a bullet-point list'
- Refine iteratively: 'Make it shorter' / 'Make it more formal'

Good practice:
- Stay in one conversation for related tasks
- Start a new conversation for unrelated topics (context from old topics can confuse Claude)

Challenge: Start a conversation where you ask Claude to write a short bio for a fictional person, then ask it to rewrite it in three different tones: formal, casual, and humorous.

lessons.title: Practical Use Cases
lessons.content:
Congratulations — you've completed Claude for Beginners!

Here are practical ways to use Claude every day:

For work:
- Draft and edit emails
- Summarise long documents
- Write job descriptions or proposals
- Generate meeting agendas

For learning:
- Explain concepts you don't understand
- Quiz yourself on any topic
- Get step-by-step explanations

For creativity:
- Brainstorm ideas
- Write first drafts
- Get feedback on your writing

For productivity:
- Create checklists and plans
- Break down complex tasks
- Organise your thoughts

Next step: Pick one task from your real life this week and try to do it with Claude's help. Start small — the habit builds fast.

Thank you for training with Greenfield Training!
